## Rule (DECODED — ARC-GEN `task_ae4f1146.py`, 2026-06-11 worker-9)

Grid is always **9×9**, colors strictly **{0 bg, 8 cyan, 1 blue}**. Four non-overlapping
(corners may touch) solid **3×3 cyan boxes** are placed at random `randint(0,6)` positions
(genuinely sliding — NOT on a 3i/3j grid). Blue pixels are sprinkled inside boxes; the
generator gives each box a DISTINCT blue count (`sample(range(9),4)` → 4 distinct lengths).
**Output = the 3×3 box with the most blue pixels** (the strict-max box, unique by
construction). Output grid is that box's colors.

Equivalent sliding-window form (matches Boladi LIVE exactly): over all 49 sliding 3×3
windows (top-left r,c ∈ 0..6), keep the **solid** ones (all 9 cells non-bg ⇒ a box), pick
the window with max blue count, reading-order (ArgMax-over-49) tiebreak. Verified
**byte-equal to LIVE on the full 200,267-pair corpus**.

## Algorithm sketch
```
crop = grid[:9,:9]                          # 9x9, fully active (no padding cells)
blue = (crop==1); bg = (crop==0)
blue_win = conv3x3_ones(blue)               # 7x7 per-window blue count
bg_win   = conv3x3_ones(bg)                 # 7x7 per-window bg count
solid    = bg_win < 0.5                      # window has 0 bg => it's a box
score    = where(solid, blue_win, -1)
idx      = argmax(score.flatten())           # 0..48
r,c      = idx//7, idx%7
out      = onehot(grid[r:r+3, c:c+3])        # ch1=blue, ch8=NOT blue (solid box, no bg)
```

## BREAKTHROUGH (2026-06-12 worker-271): the 1942 "byte-equal floor" was WRONG
The prior floor proof claimed the **648 B two-F32-channel read is irreducible** → ≥~1480, so 1311 unbeatable by Path-A. **Falsified by technique #98 (dilated crop-collapse Conv).**
The canonical graph **input `[1,10,30,30]` is FREE (uncounted)**. A conv reading it directly pays only its OUTPUT bytes + params — NO F32 slice landing. So:
- **conv1**: kernel `[1,10,2,2]`, `dilations=[21,21]` (21 = size−minisize = 30−9), real weights on tap (0,0) only (`W[ch1]=+1`, `W[ch0]=−16`, far taps 0). Reads the free input, emits ONE combined channel `comb = blue − 16·bg` over the 9×9 region as `[1,1,9,9]` (F32 324 B → Cast F16 162 B). **The 648 B slice is gone.**
- **conv2**: dense `[1,1,3,3]` ones over `comb` → `[1,1,7,7]` = `blue_count − 16·bg_count` per window. Solid windows (bg=0) outrank all straddling windows; ArgMax-over-49 picks the unique max-blue box.
- **Extraction is free of a 2nd read**: inside the winning SOLID box every cell is blue(comb=+1) or cyan(comb=0), so `blue ⟺ comb > 0.5`. Gather the 3×3 from `comb`, threshold → BOOL one-hot, Concat+Pad to `[1,10,30,30]`.

This folds blue-count + solidity + extraction onto ONE materialized channel (techniques #98 + #100). Memory 990 (dominators: comb_f32 324, comb F16 162, score 98, score_flat 98, out block 90). **cost 1136 < 1311 by 175.**

## Cost analysis — SUPERSEDED (the 1942 floor below was disproven by v11 #98; kept for provenance)
> The reasoning below assumed a `Slice`-based F32 channel read was mandatory. It is NOT — a conv reads the free input directly (see BREAKTHROUGH above). Current floor is now bounded by the combined-channel landing (`[1,1,9,9]` F32 324 + F16 162) + the 49-window score + the BOOL output block. v11 = 1136.

### (historical) why 1942 was thought to be the byte-equal FLOOR
Charged memory is dominated by reading channels out of the **F32 [1,10,30,30] input**:
- `Slice` preserves dtype, so each 9×9 channel crop lands as **[1,1,9,9] F32 = 324 B**.
- The rule provably needs **two** channels: **blue** (for the scan score AND the output
  extraction) and a **solidity** channel (bg or cyan) to reject windows that straddle two
  boxes. Blue-only ArgMax fails 5/267 (truth<100%) — measured, see Don't-do. So the F32
  read floor is **648 B**, irreducible.
- v4 then runs the conv/score/extract pipeline in F16 (counts 0..9 are exact in F16) →
  five 7×7/49-vectors at 98 B each + BOOL [1,10,3,3] output block (90 B). The F16 cast of
  the two crops costs 324 B (162×2) but saves ~560 B downstream — net −238 vs all-F32 (v6).

Even a hypothetical pipeline with *free* downstream still pays 648 (reads) + ≥196 (one
conv map) + ≥196 (second conv for solidity) + ~98 (score) + ~98 (flat) + ~50 (idx) +
~150 (extract+BOOL block) ≈ **~1480 floor**, above Aditya's **1311**. Aditya's 1311 is
therefore NOT a byte-equal reproduction of this argmax graph — it is an independent
truth-correct construction using a cheaper op mix we could not reconstruct from the LIVE
extract. **A byte-equal Path-A candidate cannot reach <1311; staging 1942 is 0-EV (the
scored value is already Aditya 1311). VERDICT: DROP, not staged.**

## Don't-do log
- **Blue-only ArgMax (drop the solidity channel)**: FAILS 5/267 — windows straddling two
  boxes' blue edges out-score the true box. Solidity is mandatory. (re-measured 2026-06-12,
  still 5/267.) BUT blue+solidity fold onto ONE combined channel `blue−16·bg` (v11) — you do
  NOT need two separate reads. The old "648 B two-crop read floor" claim is RETRACTED: a
  dilated conv reads the free input, no slice (see BREAKTHROUGH / v11).
- **RETRACTED — "the 648 B F32 two-channel slice read is irreducible"** (was the basis of the
  1942 floor / 1311-unbeatable claim). Wrong: technique #98 dilated crop-collapse conv reads
  the FREE input and lands only `[1,1,9,9]`. Never `Slice` the multi-channel input when a conv
  can crop-collapse it.
- **Disjoint-9-block simplification** (only check boxes at (3i,3j)): WRONG — boxes are placed
  at arbitrary `randint(0,6)`; 200/267 answers come from a non-(3i,3j) sliding window; 813
  solid windows sit off the disjoint grid. Must scan all 49. (`_rule2.py`.)
- **Dynamic Slice for the 3×3 extraction** (`Slice(input, starts=[r,c],…)`): rejected —
  runtime starts make `ends−starts` a `dim_param`, shape-inference can't place a static dim,
  validator drops it. Use the two-step static Gather (index length statically 3) instead.
- **F16/U8 to shrink the crops**: the F32 *landing* (slice output) is charged regardless;
  casting to F16/U8 ADDS a 162/81 B intermediate per channel. F16 only pays on the many
  downstream 49-vectors, netting −238 (v4 vs v6); it does not touch the 648 read floor.
  ConvInteger output is INT32 (196 B/7×7) — no win over F16's 98 B.
- **Combined [1,2,9,9] slice + 2→2 conv** (v5): the per-channel splits needed afterward cost
  more than two separate slices; worse (2231).
- **F16-output conv1 to kill the 324 B `comb_f32` F32 landing** (v13, the assigned w9 lever,
  2026-06-21): STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE, not a credit-probe. ORT binds `Conv`'s input and
  weight to the SAME type parameter `T`; loading `Conv(F32 input, F16 weight)` fails hard with
  `Type Error: Type parameter (T) of Optype (Conv) bound to different types (tensor(float) and
  tensor(float16))`. The #77 F16-Conv ships (080/055/143) all feed an ALREADY-F16 tensor into
  the conv — they never read the raw F32 graph input. Here conv1 reads the locked-F32 graph
  input (§INPUT-DTYPE-LOCK), so its output is forced F32. The only way to feed F16 into conv1
  is to first Cast/Slice/Gather the input, but EVERY such materialization is far larger than the
  486 B that `comb_f32`(324)+`comb`(162) cost: full-frame `Cast(input→F16)` = 18,000 B;
  `Gather` 2 channels F32 = 7,200 B. The 324 B `comb_f32` F32 landing is therefore IRREDUCIBLE
  given the F32 input + argmax-extract architecture. shape-inference reports the v13 conv output
  as F32 (324 B) anyway — it derives Conv output dtype from the input, ignoring the weight.
- **Drop the F16 `comb` cast, run all-F32 downstream** (re-measured 2026-06-21): WORSE by +106 B.
  Keeping comb_f32(324) and feeding it directly to conv2 makes score/score_flat/c_r/c_blk all F32
  (196+196+108+36) vs the F16 path (162 cast + 98+98+54+18). The F16 cast pays for itself; v12's
  comb-reuse (one 162 B F16 tensor serves BOTH conv2 scoring AND box extraction) is at the floor.
- **#96 fuse conv1+conv2 → single raw→score conv** (re-analysed 2026-06-21): deletes
  comb_f32(324)+comb(162)=486, but extraction then has no materialized blue channel to Gather
  from → must re-read the input via dynamic Slice → [1,10,3,3] F32 = 720 B (or a fresh
  single-tap conv re-lands 324 B). Net ≥ +234. v12's dual-use of `comb` (score input AND
  extraction source) is exactly what fusing throws away. Confirmed dead-end.
- **U8/QLinearConv for score/comb**: the straddle-rejection needs the signed −16·bg penalty;
  U8 cannot hold negatives so solid-vs-straddle windows become indistinguishable (§8f: F16 is
  the dtype floor for any conv carrying the signed combined signal). Dead.
